checks.finding: The write MECHANISM for a Block that publishes only a minimal/sole Resolver Evidence record is under-determined, and the two available readings produce observably different implementations. requirements.md REQ-001 step (m) (:333) states that 'on any Block reached at (0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m), this same transactional mechanism writes only Resolver Evidence's own record of that Block', and REQ-004 (:560-565) states Evidence is written 'via the identical staged-generation/journaled-transactional-publication mechanism REQ-001 fixes for every other artifact ... Resolver Evidence is not exempt from that mechanism'; Security Boundaries (:1169-1171) repeats 'No artifact this invocation stages ever reaches a live path except via the journaled publication transaction'. Against that, Main Workflows 4 (:1018-1019) specifies for the step-(a) disabled-legacy Block 'minimal Resolver Evidence written directly (no staging area ever exists in this branch)', where 'staging area' is the term Security Boundaries (:1149-1151) uses for the transaction's own transient specs/<feature>/.resolver-staging/ journal/pre-image directory. Downstream failure mode: a Phase-2 implementer and the fixture author for the step-(0) publication-journal-recovery Block and the step-(a) disabled-legacy Block cannot decide whether those branches create .resolver-staging/, write a journal and rename (torn-write-resistant, but a second journal for a --feature whose existing journal REQ-002's publication-journal-recovery row has just declared unconvergeable) or write the Evidence file straight to its live path; no acceptance criterion discriminates (AC-038's staged-generation lock, :850, names only lite-check-source-undefined/output-schema-validation-failed/snapshot-generation-mismatch). This is spec-level, not design-level: all four conflicting statements are normative sentences inside requirements.md, so the design reviewer would have to pick one. Major rather than Critical because the fail-closed outcome itself (Block, exit 1, no Manifest/Summary/Projection) is unambiguous either way. Two Minor observations recorded here without effect on this result: REQ-002's artifact-publication-failed row (:369) forbids 'a nineteenth diagnostic-id value of its own' in an enum the same REQ closes at sixteen rows (:346, AC-010, AC-014, TEST-010/TEST-014); and REQ-004's 'sole exception' (:556) reads against REQ-002's 'two named exceptions' (:383-388), reconciled only by AC-012 (:824) and TEST-012 (acceptance-tests.md:61) spelling out that one exception writes a minimal record and the other writes nothing.

For the publication-journal-recovery Block, this package asserts both that Resolver Evidence is fully written to a live path and that no live path changes, and it binds both assertions to the same fixture. Written-side: REQ-002's Evidence rule (requirements.md:383-388) names exactly two exceptions (disabled-legacy-invocation and the self-referential output-schema-validation-failed case) and publication-journal-recovery is not one of them; AC-012 (:824) repeats that scope; Security Boundaries (:1169-1177) states every live path is left 'fully absent, fully unchanged ... or (Resolver Evidence only, on a Block reached before publication) fully written', and this Block is reached at REQ-001 step (0), before publication; REQ-001 step (m) (:333) lists (0) among the Block points where the publication mechanism 'writes only Resolver Evidence's own record of that Block'; acceptance-tests.md TEST-012 (:61) accordingly requires 'every Block fixture in TEST-010 except disabled-legacy-invocation, and except the Evidence-itself-fails sub-case' to write 'a full Resolver Evidence record', and TEST-010 (:59) enumerates publication-journal-recovery among its sixteen fixtures. Unchanged-side: acceptance-tests.md TEST-047 (:93) requires the unrecoverable-journal companion fixture to Block with publication-journal-recovery 'leaving the live state exactly as found'. These cannot both hold, because resolver-evidence.yaml is itself a member of both track-exclusive publication target sets REQ-001 step (m) fixes ('{facet-manifest.yaml, generated/project-context.resolved.json, resolver-evidence.yaml}' on full, '{capability-summary.yaml, resolver-evidence.yaml}' on lite), so writing the new Evidence record necessarily changes the live state of one of the interrupted transaction's own targets. Note that requirements.md's own AC-047 (:859) does not carry the 'exactly as found' clause, so the conflict is between requirements.md/Security Boundaries and acceptance-tests.md, and internally between TEST-012 and TEST-047. Downstream failure mode: whichever behaviour the Phase-2 implementer builds, one acceptance-test row fails by construction, and the block suite's author cannot write both assertions. This belongs to specification review because both sides are Phase-1 normative text and no design or implementation choice can satisfy both; the calibration classes an impossible acceptance criterion, and a contradiction on a fail-closed write boundary, as Critical. It is also not merely theoretical: investigation.md's own Rulings D(1)/D(2) record (:1353-1359) states that a cross-model panel raised exactly this collision ('write Resolver Evidence on the uncontained-staging Block, and do not write it'), and ruling D(2) (:1421-1430) resolved it by reverting the amendment and moving the behaviour to Phase 2 ('T-007's Resolver writes minimal Resolver Evidence directly on that Block, and no frozen document needed amending to say so') without reconciling TEST-047's 'exactly as found' assertion or authorising a direct write outside Main Workflows 4's disabled-legacy branch.

Material negative, empty, boundary and failure paths are enumerated and each carries an independently-triggerable fixture. REQ-002 closes the Block taxonomy at sixteen diagnostic ids (requirements.md:353-370) and AC-010/TEST-010 (:822; acceptance-tests.md:59) require one fixture per id plus a clean negative. Empty state: zero affected components is specified as a legitimate non-Block empty resolution with its own exact-set consequence for trigger_evaluations[] (Edge Cases :1039-1058; AC-018/TEST-018). Boundary and race states: pre-publication TOCTOU including affected_components set difference with ownership_digest parity (AC-040/AC-048), the post-recheck race with journal rollback (AC-049), crash between renames plus the unrecoverable-journal case (AC-047), in-process publication failure with journal-based rollback rather than unlink (AC-039). Failure modes of every dependency subprocess are covered by named ids (canonicalizer-invocation-failed, dependency-subprocess-failed, dependency-output-malformed) and AC-057/AC-058 add the two sub-trigger isolations. Dual-artifact scope of output-schema-validation-failed is fixtured on both sides (AC-055/TEST-055) and diagnostics[] warn/block cardinality including the abort exception is fixtured (AC-056/TEST-056). Two documented, reasoned coverage carve-outs are acceptable rather than gaps: TEST-009 records that the required-present-empty Lite state has no fixture because Epic A2's frozen lite_policy schema (additionalProperties:false, sub-keys {eligible, upgrade_reasons}) admits no required_lite_checks key today, and AC-035/036/037 are registration-commit facts with a recorded manual verification. The publication-journal-recovery Evidence behaviour is reported under CONTRADICTION as a conflict, not counted again here as a coverage hole.

Each assumption is either resolved by investigation or carries an explicit pre-implementation decision with a named fallback. requirements.md Assumptions (:1207-1230): the four sibling contracts landing unmodified is tied to their recorded Spec-Review-Status: Passed state (investigation.md INV-002) with a stated follow-up-edit obligation if any changes materially; the resolve-project-context protected-suffix reservation is stated as possibly-not-yet-live with an explicit re-verification step and an alternative sequencing (INV-003); the SKILL.md unprotected status is explicitly a re-verified live snapshot, not a guarantee (INV-017). Open Questions (:1234-1252) are each dispositioned: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are deferred to a named future caller/epic and are also recorded as Non-goals (:760-762), and OQ-003 is recorded as resolved by INV-020 with a concrete file:line anchor plus the AC-053 fingerprint mechanism. Risks (:1256-1348) name owners rather than leaving open decisions: the required_lite_checks gap is assigned to Epic A2's maintainers as a named prerequisite for Epic A6's required-enforcement Lite path, and the A4/A2 addendum candidates are named with their citations and explicitly left un-actioned as outside this package's authority. No unresolved assumption is left implicit in a Goal or acceptance criterion.

The governance and irreversible-change boundaries this package implies are stated and testable. Protected-path boundary: Roles and Permissions (requirements.md:931-960) makes the future implementer the writer of the three scripts' code only, staged under specs/<feature>/human-copy/ for human application via apply-human-copy, never a direct agent write to the protected live path, and explicitly separates that from Resolver-written generated artifacts. Scope boundary: Non-goals (:771-776) and AC-032/TEST-032 lock that no file under plugins/** is modified by this package's commits, verified by git diff --stat over both registration commits (acceptance-tests.md:130-133). The human-action boundary is surfaced rather than hidden in AC-026's status ('Planned (Status resolves through a human cp action for the test.yml portion)'). Amendment-approval boundary: investigation.md's ## Amendment Re-Review Context (:792) meets the calibration's evidence bar for every ruling in the chain, including D(1)/D(2) — full commit hashes (fa1ad0e01d54be9c7e0a2d58e1064a8a9bfa9f6e, c6f6242bd49cf8dadb507ed2d7759cc955588e37, c44d056de286acc5afc4753722f47a3f72e1bac7), verbatim dated approvals ('4' and 'B: 例外を撤回し直接書く（推奨）', both 2026-08-27, with the option text each answered), and per-document SHA-256 at c44d056d whose requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md values I re-verified against this invocation's own hash-verified manifest (6567b503... and 820ee5f6...). Two Minor record-hygiene observations, neither a governance failure and neither changing this result: (a) :1423-1427 states that requirements.md, acceptance-tests.md and design.md 'return byte-for-byte to the bytes attempt 5 reviewed and PASSED — 1028bf2c…, a9fa4f89… and 3af36f44… respectively', which holds for design.md but not for the other two at that same commit, since the immediately following paragraph (:1432-1446) discloses that c44d056d also added the AC-057/AC-058 rows and removed the stray blank line — the authoritative pin subsection (:1462-1471) is correct and the disclosure is explicit, so the record is reconcilable but the sentence should be scoped to the revert component; (b) :1353-1359 refers to 'the round-5 cross-model panel on T-007' with no commit or SHA-256, where the C(1)/C(2) entry pinned its equivalent panel verdict files. The counts claim at :1443-1445 (58 criteria, 55 test rows, difference exactly the three Global rows) reconciles exactly against both documents.

Apart from the single behaviour reported under CONTRADICTION and AMBIGUITY, the package requires no invention of product behaviour downstream. Every REQ-001..REQ-008 goal has at least one acceptance criterion; requirements.md carries 58 contiguous AC rows (AC-001..AC-058, no gap or duplicate) and acceptance-tests.md carries 55 contiguous in-table TEST rows (AC-001..AC-034, AC-038..AC-058, lines 50-104 with no intervening blank), the difference being exactly the three Global rows AC-035/036/037 the preamble documents as its one exception class, so the declared 1:1 AC↔TEST mapping now holds in both directions and the Requirement column agrees row-for-row between the two documents. The revert left no dangling text I could find: no residue of the withdrawn third exception ('uncontained', 'publication write set', 'three named exceptions') exists in requirements.md or acceptance-tests.md; REQ-002's Evidence rule reads 'two named exceptions'; the diagnostic-id enum is consistently sixteen across REQ-002, REQ-004's diagnostics[] id constraint, REQ-006 item (e), AC-010, AC-014 and TEST-010/TEST-014; the ten-suite count reconciles against the ten distinct tests/*.tests.sh families named in acceptance-tests.md and against REQ-006/AC-026; TEST-047's restored 'leaving the live state exactly as found' wording is the pre-amendment form, consistent with a full revert. The two newly-added rows are consistent with the REQ-002 rows citing them: AC-057 matches the snapshot-generation-mismatch row's second, detection-only step-(e) trigger site and TEST-057's registry-swapped-during-validation fixture (exit 1, canonical detail sentence, empty capability_evaluations, no live artifact); AC-058 matches the dependency-output-malformed row's absent-component sub-trigger and TEST-058's affected-component-absent-from-context fixture (Block before any predicate evaluation, never a defaulted-empty-properties evaluation). Readiness is therefore contingent only on closing the two findings above, which require choosing between options already written in this package rather than authoring new behaviour.
